messages:
incident-bot: Pager Alert - KV_CACHE_EVICTION_SURGE detected in us-west-2 at 2026-03-15T08:13:30Z. Incident INC-2026-534 created. Symptoms: eviction rate >2000/s, paging I/O spike, increased latency on streaming endpoints. Suspected correlate: continuous-batching rollout to runtime pool 'dedicated-pool-4' (~batch_window_ms=400).

maya oncall: I'm on it. looking at evictions and paging metrics now. any customers reporting errors? I'll check tracing and run heap snapshots.

chris-runtime: FYI we pushed a batch config bump in the canary at 07:58 UTC, then to ~40% at 08:05. batch_window_ms went 120->400. Early signals showed higher throughput but the KV cache retention went up, looks like more keys per batch persisted. Also seeing streaming stalls (token cadence pauses) in the same pools, maybe partial flush + increased KV retention is pinning memory.

maya oncall: grabbing quick numbers:
```
evictions/sec: 2380
kv_cache.entries: 1.2M -> 9.8M
kv_cache.size_mb: 12GB -> 98GB
paging_io_iops: 1200 -> 4200
```

maya oncall: immediate mitigation proposal: revert batch_window_ms to 120 on affected runtime pool, enable eviction_throttle (allow short-term bracketing), set max_cache_size to 32GB. Applying now.

eng-deck: also recommend enabling kv_bloom_filter=true as a hot-toggle to reduce key-scans. we'll stage the change to one node first.

chris-runtime: rolling revert patch to config map now:
```
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap batching-config-dedicated-pool-4 --type merge -p '{"data":{"batch_window_ms":"120","eviction_throttle":"true","max_cache_size_mb":"32768"}}'
```

incident-bot: Change detected / configmap patched by chris-runtime at 2026-03-15T08:21:09Z. Auto-run: reload config on pool nodes.

maya oncall: monitoring — evictions down to ~140/s after config apply (t+3m). paging IO trending down. latency for streaming endpoints still elevated but improving. keeping throttle in place for 15m.

sam-ops: customer impact: three customers reported elevated latency and intermittent 502s on streaming calls between 08:05-08:24 UTC: cust-102 (prod), cust-214 (staging->prod route), cust-330 (prod). No data exfiltration. Support notified and we opened tickets with priority.

chris-runtime: quick note on streaming partial-flush: root cause appears to be flush-after-batch logic not firing when batch_window_ms exceeds threshold due to an edge-case that interacts with KV paging backpressure. we've put a guard to force flush on batch size/timeouts as a follow-up patch.

maya oncall: handoff — wrapping up initial mitigation. Things stable but we'll need a follow-up rollback plan + postmortem. Handover to diana-sre for the next 3 hours to run longer-run tests and coordinate with product on customer comms. tagging diana-sre @diana-sre

diana-sre: taking over. Key actions I'll run: (1) run 1h regression harness on dedicated-pool-4, (2) force-enable kv_bloom_filter across pool nodes, (3) validate streaming cadence for long contexts, (4) draft postmortem outline. I'll post status every 30m.

eng-deck: created incident doc INC-2026-534 and flagged for postmortem. assign: chris-runtime (primary), diana-sre (secondary), maya oncall (liaison).

incident-bot: Severity downgraded to SEV-3 at 2026-03-15T09:02:14Z — evictions normalized and paging within acceptable range. Monitoring will stay in verbose for 2h.

sam-ops: I'll follow up with the three customers and reference the incident doc. ETA to customers: expected update within 1h.

diana-sre: noted. adding check items for release blocking: revert batch_window_ms change from release-branch and add guarded unit tests for flush logic.

maya oncall: thanks team. leaving note and closing active command channel. if anything regresses ping @oncall.
